subject: English
passage:
The following text is from Richard Rodriguez's 1982 autobiographical work Hunger of Memory. The narrator is a young boy living in Sacramento.

I read voraciously. My father had given me access to his personal library once I could write my full name in cursive. I read and absorbed countless stories and ideas. I created a mental catalog and organized myself within it. At night before sleep I reviewed the day's literary discoveries and posed questions: What if the hero had made a different choice? How would the story change if told from another character's perspective?

©1982 by Richard Rodriguez
prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It describes the narrator trying to write his name in cursive.
choices.B: It gives instructions for how to analyze literary works.
choices.C: It portrays the narrator's relationship with his father.
choices.D: It provides examples of what the narrator thinks about at night.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it accurately describes how the underlined portion functions in the text as a whole. In the text, the narrator explains that he reads voraciously, creating a "mental catalog" of stories and ideas that he organizes in his mind. He then states that he reviews "the day's literary discoveries"—that is, reflects on his mental catalog—and poses questions about the stories he has read while lying in bed at night. The underlined portion presents two such questions (about alternative character choices and different narrative perspectives) and thus provides examples of what the narrator thinks about at night.
